title: Understanding One-hot Encoding
text: One-hot encoding is a way to represent categorical data as binary vectors. Each unique category is represented by a vector where one element is '1' (hot) and all others are '0'.

title: Calculate the Number of 6-letter Combos
text: To find the number of possible 6-letter combinations, consider that each position in the 6-letter sequence can be one of $$4$$ letters (T, G, C, A).

title: Compute the Total Number of Combinations
text: Calculate the total number of 6-letter combinations using the formula for permutations with repetition: $$4$$ to the power of $$6$$.

title: Determine the Dimensionality
text: Each 6-letter combination is a unique feature in the one-hot encoded vector. Multiply the number of 6-letter combinations by the number of positions in the DNA string that can start a 6-letter sequence.

title: Calculate the Number of Positions
text: A DNA string of $$3000$$ letters can have $$2995$$ starting positions for a 6-letter sequence $$3000-6+1$$.

title: Final Dimensionality Calculation
text: Multiply the number of 6-letter combinations by the number of starting positions to get the total dimensionality.
